text:
zoe: short follow-up from the handoff design sync. proposing a lightweight "handoff gateway" (HGW) we can run per-AZ. HGW negotiates capabilities, mints an ephemeral lease, and then either creates a TCP tunnel (fast path) or proxies (audit path). leaving notes here on teardown, opt-out, and resume semantics.

akshay: main concern is how to opt private installs out without adding manifest burden. suggest a single boolean toggle: "skip_handoff" default false. private control-planes can set it globally to true and ignore HGW entirely.

rachel: sounds good. for teardown/resume we should define a small structured frame the runtime emits before closing when it needs to evict: STREAM_EVICT {resume_token: "<opaque-signed>", reason: "quota"}. SDKs can detect STREAM_EVICT and attempt resume. older runtimes with no token should fall back to retry-from-start.

peter: security: resume_token must be PoP signed by the runtime and validated by control-plane. TTL <= 60s and single-use. HGW should never persist resume_token; validate and pass-through only. add replay-detection telemetry.

zoe: perf: HGW fast-path should do negotiate->tunnel only. proxy mode is opt-in per-tenant for audits. we need a handshake field for billing attribution so runtime knows whether traffic is hosted or dedicated even when tunneled.

akshay: sample manifest snippet (optional, very small):

skip_handoff: false  # optional; true means avoid HGW entirely

and for opt-in baggage:

handoff_billing: "hosted:lite"  # optional tag for attribution

rachel: failure modes: if HGW is unhealthy, SDKs should try direct-pinned runtime when available. hosted non-pinned tenants get routed to a control-plane fallback which may serve a lower-cost model. HGW must provide a circuit-breaker metric consumers can use to trigger client-side fallback.

peter: teardown edge: if eviction happens mid-stream, SDK reconnect+resume must aim for <250ms total disruption. if not possible, control-plane should route to a cheaper model and mark session degraded in telemetry. consider an opt-in "standby hedging" mode for very high SLA tenants (dual-write to standby) with explicit billing.

zoe: ops checklist: 1) per-AZ canary, 2) feature-flag per-tenant, 3) global kill-switch, 4) mTLS lifecycle, 5) resume_token spec, 6) privacy audit proving HGW stores no stream payloads. ops-bot created board: https://infra/boards/hgw-canary

ops-bot: task created: infra/issue/5342  includes cert rotation, canary plan, feature flagging endpoints, and dashboards.

akshay: tests I'll run: opt-out correctness, STREAM_EVICT resume+reconnect, resume_token replay attempt, fast-tunnel latency vs direct, and privacy audit.

rachel: add probe semantics: /health/hgw and /health/runtime separate endpoints; control-plane should prefer runtime health over HGW when deciding failover. probes must respect skip_handoff.

zoe: great, I'll draft a compact RFC with diagrams: handshake (billing + mode), STREAM_EVICT + token lifecycle, manifest opt-out, and canary plan. please flag if we missed anything. thanks! :rocket:
